Second paragraph is a flat checklist: fenced writer, sticky post-write reads, pins vs django_session, one capture per attempt_id, blank attempt_id reject, write_lsn/wal_lsn refuse, five /readyz 503 OR-gates, then failover-status.json.

Referenced operator runbook already defines sticky/lag gates, blank attempt_id, capture LSN refuse, /readyz traffic gates, dump_failover path, and the exact failover-status.json object. Ordinary runbook, not a repair map; detailed gates need not be restated as a grader inventory in instruction.md.

Solver-visible log lines corroborate the same incident claims referenced in instruction.md.

Requirement families (writer-only mutations, sticky/pin store, lag gate, fence epoch, capture idempotency, readyz, status dump/counts, sync_standby, restart) remain discoverable from instruction + runbook; paragraph 2 clauses map suspiciously one-to-one onto those families.
PASS requires REVERSE_OUTLINE_RISK and COMPRESSED_RUBRIC no higher than LOW. Human tests flag one-clause-per-requirement inventories and reverse-outline of verifier rows.
Synthetic-completeness and one-sentence-per-rubric-item patterns match paragraph 2; preferred human pattern is incident + operational invariants with protocol detail left in the existing runbook.
